_readme: Registry of scenario IDs whose elixcee-side outcome is expected to be something other than a plain success, read by classify-elixcee-outcomes.mjs. Every entry is a deliberate, evidence-backed claim — 'this scenario SHOULD fail this specific way, and that is correct VBA behavior, not a bug' — never an excuse to make a genuinely-broken scenario pass the CI gate. Mirrors the anti-laundering discipline compat/differential/classify.mjs's UNSUPPORTED_ALLOWLIST already documents: a new entry needs a real reason. classify-elixcee-outcomes.mjs cross-checks BOTH expectedErrorKind and expectedErrorMessage (exact string, not a substring/fuzzy match) against the actual run, so a regression that changes *how* or *why* a scenario fails still surfaces as MISMATCH rather than silently keeping the old classification. Registering a scenario as 'harness' kind (a timeout/hang/crash) here is never valid — see the script's own header.

arithmetic_0128.reason: 5 \ 0.5 — VBA's \ (integer division) rounds each operand to a whole number first via banker's rounding (round-half-to-even), not truncation. 0.5 rounds to 0 (nearest even), giving 5 \ 0 — a real division by zero, matching real VBA, not a bug.

arithmetic_0144.reason: 0.1 \ 0.2 — both operands round to 0 before the \ operator divides (0.1 and 0.2 are both closer to 0 than to 1), giving a real division by zero.

arithmetic_0158.reason: 5 Mod 0.5 — same operand-rounding rule as \ applies to Mod. 0.5 rounds to 0 (nearest even), giving 5 Mod 0 — a real division by zero.

arithmetic_0174.reason: 0.1 Mod 0.2 — both operands round to 0 before Mod divides, giving a real division by zero.

arithmetic_div_by_zero_0001.reason: 5 / 0 — a literal division by zero. Real VBA raises the same runtime error.

arithmetic_div_by_zero_0003.reason: 0 / 0 — a literal division by zero (indeterminate form still errors in real VBA, it does not produce NaN).

unsupported_functions_0001.reason: Application.WorksheetFunction.TextJoin — deliberately unimplemented worksheet function (this scenario's own category name is 'unsupported_functions'; it exists specifically to exercise the not-implemented path, not to pass).

unsupported_functions_0002.reason: Application.WorksheetFunction.Xlookup — deliberately unimplemented worksheet function, same reasoning as unsupported_functions_0001.

nondeterministic_0002.reason: Timer() is not implemented. Its own category is 'nondeterministic' (time-dependent output would make this scenario unable to have a fixed expected value even if Timer() were implemented), so leaving it unimplemented is low-value to fix and the failure is registered rather than chased.
